articles.title: A rate at an instant
articles.hook: A journey has an average velocity, but what could a rate at one instant mean?
articles.outcome: Compute secant slopes for f(x)=x² and derive its signed instantaneous rate; distinguish velocity from speed.
articles.visual: Secant lines approaching a tangent with a numerical slope table.
articles.proof: Prove the derivative of x² by cancellation and an explicit limit estimate; negative slopes are signed rates, while physical speed is absolute velocity.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The body introduces functions and secant slope, but uses coordinate pairs, division and algebraic expansion.

articles.title: A corner that defeats the derivative
articles.hook: Zooming in does not always produce a straight line.
articles.outcome: Use one-sided difference quotients to explain why |x| has no derivative at zero.
articles.visual: Two independently controlled secants at a corner.
articles.proof: Prove nonexistence from unequal one-sided limits; do not equate continuity with differentiability.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule introduces secant slope and the two-sided derivative; the entry preparation is absolute value and ordinary slope.

articles.title: The chain rule as two magnifying lenses
articles.hook: Two gentle changes can combine into a surprisingly large one.
articles.outcome: Differentiate a composition and interpret units in the result.
articles.visual: Two linked local linear maps and a composed graph.
articles.proof: Derive with first-order remainders assuming both derivatives exist; avoid a proof that divides by a possibly zero increment.

metadataProvenance.rationale: These are equivalent phrasings of the two prerequisites actually used; local remainder notation is introduced in the body.

articles.title: Area that grows while you watch
articles.hook: A graph of speed can tell the story of distance.
articles.outcome: Build lower and upper sums for a nonnegative increasing function.
articles.visual: Rectangles with an explicit upper-minus-lower gap.
articles.proof: Prove bounds for increasing continuous examples; signed area and general integrability get separate definitions.

metadataProvenance.rationale: Rectangle sums use graph heights, integer indexing and algebra; summation notation, induction and the limiting argument are explained.

articles.title: Why accumulation undoes differentiation
articles.hook: The two main inventions of calculus turn out to be partners.
articles.outcome: Explain why the derivative of accumulated continuous input equals its current value.
articles.visual: An added thin strip alongside its average height.
articles.proof: Prove using continuity and integral bounds; state continuity at the evaluation point and distinguish the two fundamental theorems.

articles.title: The average speed you must have reached
articles.hook: An average rate secretly promises an instantaneous rate somewhere.
articles.outcome: Apply the mean value theorem and identify failed hypotheses.
articles.visual: A secant shifted until tangent; endpoint and corner counterexamples.
articles.proof: Prove from Rolle's theorem with its extremum lemma stated; require continuity on [a,b] and differentiability on (a,b).

metadataProvenance.rationale: The proof invokes the extreme-value theorem without proving it from completeness.

articles.title: Substitution is a change of ruler
articles.hook: Changing coordinates changes the size of every tiny interval.
articles.outcome: Perform a definite substitution with consistent limits and orientation.
articles.visual: A stretched number line and matching signed strips.
articles.proof: Derive from the fundamental theorem under continuous f and continuously differentiable g; distinguish from an invertible coordinate formula.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The proof uses the chain rule and both fundamental-theorem directions for signed definite integrals.

articles.title: An infinite journey with finite area
articles.hook: A region can go on forever without having infinite area.
articles.outcome: Classify ∫₁∞ x^(-p)dx and separate improper limits from ordinary integrals.
articles.visual: Tail rectangles and the accumulating area as cutoff grows.
articles.proof: Compute truncated integrals and take limits; no inference from a finite plotting window.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The calculation evaluates power antiderivatives before taking an improper limit; the logarithmic case is supplied in the capsule.

articles.title: A polynomial approximation with an error receipt
articles.hook: A calculator can replace a curve with a polynomial, but how trustworthy is it?
articles.outcome: Bound the error in a local sine approximation.
articles.visual: Approximation, residual and a separate certified error envelope.
articles.proof: State Taylor's theorem with derivative hypotheses; prove an integral-remainder special case, defer general variants.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The integral-remainder induction invokes the fundamental theorem and integrates by parts; neither method is derived here.

articles.title: A smooth function its Taylor series misses
articles.hook: Knowing every derivative at a point can still miss the function nearby.
articles.outcome: Distinguish smooth from analytic using the flat exponential example.
articles.visual: Function and zero Taylor polynomial with a logarithmic-scale inset.
articles.proof: Prove exponential decay dominates powers and outline induction for all derivatives; infinite Taylor equality needs its own convergence argument.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The body distinguishes a Taylor series from its function, explains smoothness and proves the exponential-dominance estimate; coefficient notation and repeated differentiation remain preparation.

articles.title: Reading a landscape without seeing the mountain
articles.hook: A few contour lines can reveal steepness and direction.
articles.outcome: Interpret level sets and compare directional changes on a quadratic landscape.
articles.visual: Contour map paired with a keyboard-selected height table.
articles.proof: Calculate exact level sets; contour spacing depends on chosen levels and is not itself a derivative.

articles.title: A compass that points uphill
articles.hook: One arrow summarizes every first-order directional change.
articles.outcome: Calculate the gradient and find steepest ascent among unit directions.
articles.visual: Contour map with a rotatable unit arrow and derivative readout.
articles.proof: Prove steepest ascent using Cauchy–Schwarz; assume differentiability, not merely existence of partials.

articles.title: Partial derivatives can miss a cliff
articles.hook: Checking only east and north can hide what happens diagonally.
articles.outcome: Exhibit existing partials at a point without continuity there.
articles.visual: Axis and diagonal approaches with exact value tables.
articles.proof: Prove axis limits differ from diagonal limits; distinguish partials, directional derivatives and total differentiability.

articles.title: Why polar coordinates need an extra r
articles.hook: Equal steps on a polar grid do not enclose equal areas.
articles.outcome: Derive the polar area factor and use it in a disk integral.
articles.formula: dx dy=|det DΦ(r,θ)|dr dθ=r dr dθ
articles.visual: Polar cells and local parallelogram area.
articles.proof: Compute determinant and an annular-sector limit; state change-of-variables hypotheses and handle origin as an exceptional point.

articles.title: The same region, two ways to slice
articles.hook: A difficult integral can become simple when its slices turn sideways.
articles.outcome: Reverse integration order on a triangular region.
articles.visual: Horizontal and vertical slices with synchronized bounds.
articles.proof: Justify for continuous f on a compact triangle; conditional improper integrals require additional care.

articles.title: Does a round trip cost any work?
articles.hook: Two routes between the same places can have different totals.
articles.outcome: Compute a line integral and recognize a gradient field example.
articles.visual: Two selectable paths through a vector field.
articles.proof: Derive parameter formula and prove endpoint rule for F=∇φ; do not infer global conservativity from zero curl alone.

articles.title: The hole that curl cannot see
articles.hook: A field can have zero curl everywhere it exists and still do work around a loop.
articles.outcome: Use a punctured-plane field to test a missing domain hypothesis.
articles.visual: Loops enclosing or avoiding the excluded origin.
articles.proof: Compute zero scalar curl and nonzero circulation explicitly; state simply connected domain sufficiency.

articles.title: A boundary remembers the whole interior
articles.hook: Interior edges cancel, leaving a theorem on the outside.
articles.outcome: Explain and verify Green's theorem on a rectangle.
articles.visual: Tiled region with opposite interior-edge contributions.
articles.proof: Prove rectangular case using the fundamental theorem; state smoothness and orientation and defer general-region proof.

articles.title: Count the flow through a box
articles.hook: Tiny sources inside a region determine its net outward flow.
articles.outcome: Compute divergence and compare volume and boundary totals for a simple field.
articles.visual: Box faces with signed flux and interior source totals.
articles.proof: Prove rectangular-box case for C¹ fields; curved boundaries and general theorem stated.

articles.title: The same circulation from different surfaces
articles.hook: A loop can be spanned by different surfaces yet give the same answer.
articles.outcome: Check Stokes' theorem for a planar disk and explain orientation.
articles.visual: Disk and dome sharing a boundary with linked orientation arrows.
articles.proof: Work a smooth-field example exactly; state oriented-surface and boundary regularity assumptions, defer full proof.

articles.title: How close is close enough?
articles.hook: Turn approaching a value into a promise you can test.
articles.outcome: Choose a delta that guarantees an epsilon tolerance for f(x)=2x at x=1, then translate the idea to sequence tails.
articles.visual: Input delta interval linked to an output epsilon band, with exact endpoint bounds.
articles.proof: Prove the epsilon-delta claim algebraically; explain quantifier order and give 1/n as an optional epsilon-N comparison. A finite plot cannot certify all inputs.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The body proves sequence convergence of 1/n and explains sequence notation, absolute distance and quantifiers; general function preparation is unnecessary.

articles.title: The missing number in the rationals
articles.hook: A perfectly sensible sequence can approach a number its universe lacks.
articles.outcome: Explain completeness through rational approximations to √2.
articles.visual: Nested rational brackets for √2.
articles.proof: Prove irrationality and explain real least-upper-bound axiom; constructing the reals is deferred.

articles.title: A sequence cannot escape a closed box
articles.hook: Infinitely many points in a bounded interval must cluster somewhere.
articles.outcome: Construct a convergent subsequence by nested intervals.
articles.formula: Every bounded real sequence has a convergent subsequence.
articles.visual: Successive bisections retaining infinitely many points.
articles.proof: Prove Bolzano–Weierstrass in R; distinguish boundedness from convergence of the whole sequence.

articles.title: One tolerance for the whole interval
articles.hook: Local control and a single global guarantee are different promises.
articles.outcome: Compare continuity and uniform continuity for x² on bounded and unbounded domains.
articles.visual: Paired moving points with shared tolerance.
articles.proof: Prove bounded-interval Lipschitz bound and unbounded-domain failure; compactness theorem stated separately.

articles.title: When rectangle sums refuse to agree
articles.hook: Dense zeroes and ones make every rectangle uncertain.
articles.outcome: Show the rational-indicator function is not Riemann integrable.
articles.visual: Symbolic rational/irrational samples with lower/upper sums.
articles.proof: Prove using density; warn that plotted finite samples cannot show both dense sets faithfully.

articles.title: A limit can change the shape of a theorem
articles.hook: Continuous curves may converge to a discontinuous function.
articles.outcome: Distinguish pointwise and uniform convergence with x^n on [0,1].
articles.visual: Curves plus supremum-error panel.
articles.proof: Prove pointwise limit and failure of uniform convergence; prove uniform limits preserve continuity.

articles.title: Infinitely many points can have zero length
articles.hook: The rationals fill every interval yet occupy no length.
articles.outcome: Cover a countable set with intervals of arbitrarily small total length.
articles.visual: Numbered interval covers and their total length budget.
articles.proof: Prove outer measure zero for countable sets; zero measure does not imply countability.

articles.title: An uncountable set with no length
articles.hook: Removing open middle thirds leaves more points than any list can hold.
articles.outcome: Compute remaining stage lengths and explain Cantor-set uncountability.
articles.visual: Finite Cantor stages with interval count and remaining length.
articles.proof: Prove measure-zero cover and inject binary sequences via ternary digits; avoid ambiguous expansion shortcuts.

articles.title: Integrating by sorting heights
articles.hook: An integral can collect points by value rather than by position.
articles.outcome: Integrate simple functions and understand the nonnegative Lebesgue integral definition.
articles.visual: Value bins over a measurable step function.
articles.proof: Define sigma-algebra, measurability and simple integrals locally; assume Lebesgue measure construction rather than claiming to prove it.

articles.title: When may a limit pass through an integral?
articles.hook: Pointwise shrinking can hide a persistent area spike.
articles.outcome: Check dominated convergence assumptions and expose a counterexample.
articles.visual: Moving/shrinking spike contrasted with integrable domination.
articles.proof: State theorem precisely, prove a bounded finite-measure special case only with supporting lemma; full theorem proof deferred.

articles.title: Multiplication that turns the plane
articles.hook: A number can describe a turn as well as a size.
articles.outcome: Multiply complex numbers using angle and magnitude.
articles.visual: Original and multiplied vectors.
articles.proof: Prove via trigonometric addition; introduce Euler notation without assuming its analytic construction.

metadataProvenance.rationale: Coordinate multiplication and lengths use algebra and Pythagoras; the angle-addition identities are invoked without proof.

articles.title: What squaring does to a square grid
articles.hook: A familiar polynomial folds a plane in an unfamiliar way.
articles.outcome: Track modulus and argument under z² and identify two-to-one behavior.
articles.visual: Input grid and mapped curves with paired points.
articles.proof: Derive mapping algebraically; angle preservation excludes the critical point zero.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The square-map calculation uses coordinates and the polar multiplication rule recalled in its capsule.

articles.title: A derivative must agree from every direction
articles.hook: Complex differentiation demands much more than two real partial derivatives.
articles.outcome: Test z² and conjugation using directional difference quotients.
articles.visual: Difference quotient as h approaches at selectable angles.
articles.proof: Prove examples directly; finitely many approach directions cannot establish a general complex limit.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The proof compares difference quotients over every complex approach and uses modulus estimates; directional checks alone are not sufficient.

articles.title: Two equations behind rigid behavior
articles.hook: A local rotation-and-stretch map has constrained coordinates.
articles.outcome: Derive Cauchy–Riemann equations and test simple functions.
articles.visual: Local grid vectors and component derivative table.
articles.proof: Necessity derived; sufficiency stated with continuous first partials near the point, not bare equalities.

metadataProvenance.rationale: Necessity uses directional partials and sufficiency uses the total-differentiability expansion under continuous-partial assumptions.

articles.title: Why the logarithm needs a cut
articles.hook: Walking once around zero changes an angle by a full turn.
articles.outcome: Choose a logarithm branch and explain its excluded ray.
articles.visual: Loop tracking unwrapped angle and principal branch jump.
articles.proof: Prove branch inconsistency around a full circle; no global continuous log on C\{0}.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The branch construction needs a continuous choice of argument and the real logarithm; the exponential notation is explained.

articles.title: A loop that counts turns
articles.hook: Integrating 1/z detects whether a path circles a missing point.
articles.outcome: Compute a circle integral and interpret orientation.
articles.visual: Circular path and cumulative complex integral.
articles.proof: Calculate parametrically; general winding-number theorem stated with closed-curve and avoidance assumptions.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The contour-integral definition is supplied and the circle is evaluated through real parameter integration.

articles.title: The boundary knows every interior value
articles.hook: A contour of values determines a holomorphic function inside.
articles.outcome: Apply Cauchy's integral formula on a disk.
articles.visual: Boundary samples and reconstructed value for a polynomial.
articles.proof: State theorem for a positively oriented circle with f holomorphic on a neighborhood of its closed disk; derive examples, defer general proof.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The disk-case Cauchy formula is stated with its neighborhood condition; its calculation assumes contour integration and holomorphy.

articles.title: A real integral solved by a complex detour
articles.hook: A semicircle can simplify an integral along the real line.
articles.outcome: Evaluate ∫R 1/(1+x²)dx using one residue and an arc bound.
articles.visual: Real segment, upper arc, pole and vanishing arc bound.
articles.proof: State residue theorem and prove this example's arc tends to zero; never drop an arc without an estimate.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The residue and arc estimate connect a contour integral with two separately convergent real tails.

articles.title: Why the biggest value lives on the edge
articles.hook: A holomorphic function cannot form an isolated interior peak in magnitude.
articles.outcome: Use the maximum-modulus principle on a disk.
articles.visual: Modulus contours with boundary/interior comparison.
articles.proof: Prove a local mean-value consequence and state full principle; apply only when holomorphic inside and continuous on closed disk.

metadataProvenance.rationale: Compactness supplies an attained maximum, the Cauchy mean-value formula and triangle equality give local constancy, and the identity theorem is invoked for global constancy.

articles.title: A distant singularity limits a local series
articles.hook: A series around zero can sense a singularity it never reaches.
articles.outcome: Find radii of convergence for geometric and rational examples.
articles.visual: Disk of convergence with singularities and partial-sum error.
articles.proof: Prove geometric series and selected expansions; general nearest-singularity principle needs analytic-continuation qualifications.

metadataProvenance.rationale: Finite geometric sums prove the worked radii and tail bounds; general Cauchy coefficient theory is optional continuation.

articles.title: The mathematics of a cooling cup
articles.hook: A simple rule predicts a whole temperature curve.
articles.outcome: Solve a constant-ambient cooling model and interpret its time scale.
articles.visual: Temperature curve with ambient asymptote.
articles.proof: Verify solution and initial value; model assumptions exclude changing ambient temperature and phase changes.

articles.title: Read a differential equation without solving it
articles.hook: Tiny slope marks reveal possible futures.
articles.outcome: Sketch solutions and identify an equilibrium from y'=1−y.
articles.visual: Static slope field with optional stepped trajectory.
articles.proof: Use sign analysis and verify exact solutions; sketching is qualitative evidence, not existence proof.

articles.title: Growth that runs out of room
articles.hook: Unchecked exponential growth becomes an S-curve when resources matter.
articles.outcome: Analyze logistic equilibria, stability and inflection.
articles.visual: Population curves and phase line.
articles.proof: Derive positive solution and stability by signs; carry capacity is a model parameter, not a universal ecological law.

articles.title: One starting point, several futures
articles.hook: A continuous rule need not select a unique trajectory.
articles.outcome: Construct delayed solutions of y'=2√|y| at y(0)=0.
articles.visual: Multiple exact trajectories through the origin.
articles.proof: Verify differentiability and equation at join; state local Lipschitz sufficient condition and defer general existence proof.

articles.title: Three ways a spring can settle
articles.hook: Changing one damping parameter alters the character of motion.
articles.outcome: Classify underdamped, critical and overdamped linear oscillators.
articles.visual: Displacement and phase portrait with discriminant label.
articles.proof: Solve characteristic equation for positive m,k and c≥0; ideal linear spring assumptions stated.

articles.title: When a small push keeps adding up
articles.hook: A well-timed repeated push can produce a large response.
articles.outcome: Distinguish undamped resonance from a finite damped frequency response.
articles.visual: Forcing and response with an amplitude envelope.
articles.proof: Derive resonant particular solution; do not imply damping leaves unbounded response.

articles.title: Eigenvalues draw a phase portrait
articles.hook: A matrix can predict spirals, saddles and straight approaches.
articles.outcome: Classify representative planar linear systems.
articles.visual: Phase plane with eigenvectors and trajectories.
articles.proof: Prove diagonalizable examples; defective matrices and nonlinear extrapolation require further arguments.

articles.title: Where a local approximation stops deciding
articles.hook: A zero eigenvalue can hide opposite kinds of stability.
articles.outcome: Compare x'=−x³ and x'=x³ and explain inconclusive linearization.
articles.visual: Matched linearization with contrasting nonlinear phase lines.
articles.proof: Prove scalar stability from signs; state hyperbolic linearization principle without full proof.

articles.title: A tiny parameter change can erase equilibrium
articles.hook: Two resting states can collide and disappear.
articles.outcome: Find equilibria and stability in a saddle-node normal form.
articles.visual: Parameter-equilibrium diagram with stable and unstable branches.
articles.proof: Derive branches and stability for the scalar model; generic bifurcation theory deferred.

articles.title: Simple repetition, complicated futures
articles.hook: Repeatedly applying one quadratic can resist long-term prediction.
articles.outcome: Analyze fixed-point stability and separate numerical chaos evidence from proof.
articles.visual: Cobweb and finite bifurcation samples.
articles.proof: Prove fixed-point stability in stated parameter ranges; period-doubling universality and chaos claims remain referenced results.

articles.title: Why a computer loses a tiny number
articles.hook: Adding a small quantity to a large one can change nothing.
articles.outcome: Explain finite precision using a small decimal floating-point model.
articles.formula: fl(a+b) may equal a even when b≠0
articles.visual: Toy precision selector and exact/rounded arithmetic table.
articles.proof: Prove toy-model examples; distinguish the model from binary IEEE arithmetic and avoid universal relative error at underflow.

articles.title: Two equal formulas, unequal answers
articles.hook: Algebraically identical expressions can behave differently on a machine.
articles.outcome: Rationalize √(1+x)−1 to reduce cancellation.
articles.visual: Relative-error comparison against a high-accuracy reference.
articles.proof: Prove identity on x≥−1 and analyze small positive x; reference accuracy must be specified.

articles.title: A bad problem or a bad algorithm?
articles.hook: An accurate calculation cannot repair data that determine the answer weakly.
articles.outcome: Distinguish conditioning from computational stability with scalar examples.
articles.visual: Input perturbations and resulting output ranges.
articles.proof: Derive first-order relative sensitivity away from zero; finite perturbation bounds are separate.

articles.title: A root you can trap
articles.hook: Repeated halving turns uncertainty into a certified interval.
articles.outcome: Run bisection and choose iterations for a requested bracket width.
articles.visual: Bracket history and sign table.
articles.proof: Prove bracket invariant using intermediate value theorem; continuity and reliable signs are necessary.

articles.title: Newton's method can leap the wrong way
articles.hook: A fast root finder can converge beautifully or fail spectacularly.
articles.outcome: Compute Newton steps and diagnose a cycle or zero derivative.
articles.visual: Tangent steps and residual table with bisection comparison.
articles.proof: Derive iteration and local quadratic error under a simple-root smoothness hypothesis; no global guarantee.

articles.title: Why a smaller step can give a worse derivative
articles.hook: Approximation and rounding pull a computation in opposite directions.
articles.outcome: Balance truncation and roundoff in a finite difference.
articles.visual: Error-versus-step plot with model envelope.
articles.proof: Derive truncation term and discuss rounding model assumptions; constants and noisy data alter optimal h.

articles.title: Counting area with a known error
articles.hook: Rectangles improve when curvature is taken seriously.
articles.outcome: Apply composite trapezoidal quadrature with a certified smooth-function bound.
articles.visual: Trapezoids, true area and error bound.
articles.proof: State/prove single-panel remainder and sum bounds for C² functions; singular integrands need different methods.

articles.title: More points can make an interpolant worse
articles.hook: High-degree polynomial fitting can oscillate near the edges.
articles.outcome: Compare equally spaced and Chebyshev nodes on Runge's function.
articles.visual: Node distribution and endpoint errors.
articles.proof: Demonstrate failure and explain node geometry; finite plots are not proof of asymptotic convergence.

articles.title: A decaying equation with an exploding computation
articles.hook: The numerical solution can grow while the exact solution shrinks.
articles.outcome: Derive Euler's stability restriction on a decay equation.
articles.visual: Exact decay and numerical points across step sizes.
articles.proof: Prove scalar stability for λ>0; convergence, accuracy and stability are distinct.

articles.title: Fit a line without squaring the trouble
articles.hook: Two least-squares methods can amplify errors differently.
articles.outcome: Form a small least-squares problem and explain the numerical appeal of QR.
articles.visual: Nearly dependent columns with residual and coefficient sensitivity.
articles.proof: Derive full-column-rank QR reduction and condition identity; QR does not fix intrinsic ill-conditioning.

articles.title: The best box from a sheet of card
articles.hook: A familiar craft problem hides an optimization model.
articles.outcome: Form a volume function, identify its feasible interval and compare candidates.
articles.visual: Cut-out sheet and volume graph with endpoints.
articles.proof: Derive model and use derivative for a square sheet; physical thickness and waste are intentionally omitted.

articles.title: A valley is not always the deepest valley
articles.hook: Stopping downhill does not certify the best destination.
articles.outcome: Distinguish local minima, global minima and stationary points.
articles.formula: f'(x*)=0 is necessary for an interior differentiable local minimum
articles.visual: Multi-valley graph with candidate points.
articles.proof: Give explicit polynomial examples; endpoints and nondifferentiable minima need separate checks.

articles.title: The special promise of a convex bowl
articles.hook: Some landscapes let a local answer settle a global question.
articles.outcome: Check convexity and prove every local minimum is global.
articles.visual: Chord versus graph with movable endpoints.
articles.proof: Prove local-to-global theorem on a convex domain; strict convexity gives at most one minimizer, not existence.

articles.title: How long should a downhill step be?
articles.hook: Stepping downhill too far can send you uphill.
articles.outcome: Analyze gradient descent on a positive quadratic.
articles.visual: Contour map and iteration path with objective table.
articles.proof: For a positive-definite quadratic with Hessian Q, prove e_{k+1}=(I−αQ)e_k and contraction factor max_i|1−αλ_i|<1 when 0<α<2/λmax. This is geometric convergence of iterates, not quadratic convergence; state the general smooth descent lemma separately.

articles.title: An optimum pressed against a fence
articles.hook: At a constrained optimum, the best direction may be forbidden.
articles.outcome: Solve a regular equality-constrained problem with multipliers.
articles.visual: Level sets touching a constraint.
articles.proof: Derive tangent-space condition when ∇g≠0; multiplier solutions are candidates, not automatic minima.

articles.title: Why the best mix often sits at a corner
articles.hook: A resource-allocation picture turns into a geometric theorem.
articles.outcome: Solve a bounded two-variable linear program and identify multiple optima.
articles.visual: Feasible polygon with moving objective line.
articles.proof: Prove optimum occurs at some vertex for a nonempty bounded polytope; unbounded sets and absent vertices require qualifications.

articles.title: A second problem certifies the first
articles.hook: You can prove a candidate is nearly optimal without knowing the exact optimum.
articles.outcome: Construct a Lagrangian lower bound and compute a duality gap.
articles.formula: g(λ)=inf_x L(x,λ)≤p*, λ≥0 for inequality multipliers
articles.visual: Primal candidate and dual bound narrowing a gap.
articles.proof: Prove weak duality; strong duality requires additional assumptions and is not universal.

articles.title: Constraints that matter and constraints that rest
articles.hook: A constraint can be present without determining the optimum.
articles.outcome: Check KKT conditions for a simple convex constrained problem.
articles.visual: Active constraints and multipliers with residuals.
articles.proof: State primal/dual feasibility, stationarity and complementarity; convexity gives sufficiency, constraint qualifications govern necessity.

articles.title: A minimum with no derivative
articles.hook: The sharp point of absolute value still has a useful notion of slope.
articles.outcome: Find subgradients and explain why a median minimizes absolute deviations.
articles.formula: g∈∂f(x) iff f(y)≥f(x)+g(y−x) for all y
articles.visual: Supporting lines at a corner and absolute-loss graph.
articles.proof: Prove ∂|x|(0)=[−1,1] and median characterization; ties can yield an interval of minimizers.

articles.title: Use curvature to choose a better step
articles.hook: A narrow valley defeats equal steps but offers information in its curvature.
articles.outcome: Derive Newton's optimization step and identify failure outside convex neighborhoods.

labs.pitfalls: At zero speed curvature formula is undefined; graph appearance depends on aspect ratio.
labs.accessibleFallback: Numeric derivative table, formula substitution and named regularity status.

labs.title: Sphere path measurer
labs.readout: Metric coefficients, path length estimate, exact great-circle central angle when applicable.
labs.invariant: For sphere radius R, great-circle arc length is R times central angle for the shorter arc.
labs.pitfalls: Latitude circles except equator are not geodesics; coordinate poles are singular.
labs.accessibleFallback: Coordinate-free dot-product central-angle calculation and a segment-length table.

labs.title: Polynomial zero-set explorer
labs.readout: Residual F(x,y), gradient when defined, exact special-point checks.
labs.invariant: Displayed real points satisfy F=0 to stated numerical tolerance; exact named examples use symbolic substitution.
labs.pitfalls: Pixel absence is not proof of no zeros; near singularities numerical gradients mislead.
labs.accessibleFallback: Preset equations, symbolic sample calculations and a coordinate table of verified points.

labs.title: Line and conic intersections
labs.readout: Roots, discriminant, homogeneous point at infinity and intersection multiplicity for the preset tangency.
labs.invariant: Line and conic have total intersection multiplicity two over complex projective plane if no component is shared.
labs.pitfalls: Real affine plot can hide complex or infinite intersections; the full Bézout theorem is not proved by the widget.
labs.accessibleFallback: Exact polynomial elimination and roots table with multiplicity and chart labels.

labs.title: Commuting diagram checker
labs.readout: Both path outputs for every element and the first mismatch.
labs.invariant: A finite-set square commutes iff the two composites agree on every input element.
labs.pitfalls: One tested element cannot establish equality of functions; arrow domains/codomains must match.
labs.accessibleFallback: Fully keyboard-controlled function tables with a row-by-row equality verdict.

labs.title: Pullback matching table
controls: functions f and g as tables
labs.readout: All pairs (x,y) with f(x)=g(y), projection maps and candidate mediator.
labs.invariant: The Set pullback contains exactly compatible pairs and each compatible cone has a unique mediator.
labs.pitfalls: Database join analogy omits bag semantics and missing values; avoid claiming all joins are pullbacks.
labs.accessibleFallback: Text matching-pair table and stepwise universal-property proof using an arbitrary element.

labs.title: Reveal the denominator
labs.readout: Frequency tree, exact posterior and simulated estimate
labs.invariant: Posterior probabilities sum to 1; empirical frequencies approach values only with enough independent draws
labs.pitfalls: A likelihood is not a posterior; zero-probability evidence cannot be conditioned on
labs.accessibleFallback: Full branch-count table, formulas, keyboard controls and static worked cases

labs.title: Build a fair or lopsided game
labs.readout: Exact expectation and variance beside simulated running averages
labs.invariant: Probabilities sum to 1; exact mean is unchanged by trial count
labs.pitfalls: A small simulation can wander far from expectation
labs.accessibleFallback: Data table, exact arithmetic and downloadable text transcript

labs.title: Watch interval coverage
labs.readout: Intervals that cover fixed parameter, observed coverage and nominal target
labs.invariant: Coverage claim concerns the method under its sampling assumptions
labs.pitfalls: A realized interval is not assigned a 95% posterior probability
labs.accessibleFallback: Text list of intervals with cover/miss flags and summary counts

labs.title: Explore null tails and selection
labs.readout: Exact binomial tail and simulated minimum p-value distribution
labs.invariant: Exact null distribution normalized to 1
labs.pitfalls: p-value is not P(null true); choosing direction afterward changes the test; the exact familywise formula requires independent uniform null p-values.
labs.accessibleFallback: Exact probability table, keyboard tail selection and text histogram

labs.title: Walk until an edge
labs.readout: Exact finite hitting probability and sampled paths
labs.invariant: Absorbing states remain absorbing; probabilities total 1
labs.pitfalls: Finite runs cannot establish eventual absorption or exact probability
labs.accessibleFallback: Path table, recurrence solution and pauseable step controls

labs.title: Playlist mood chain
labs.readout: Distribution by step and stationary candidate
labs.invariant: Every transition row sums to 1; distribution stays normalized
labs.pitfalls: Stationarity does not ensure convergence when chain is periodic or reducible
labs.accessibleFallback: Transition table, iteration table and plain-language state descriptions

labs.title: Mix an alphabet
labs.readout: Surprise bars, entropy and conditional entropy
labs.invariant: Probabilities sum to 1; H(X,Y)=H(X)+H(Y|X)
labs.pitfalls: Observed sample frequencies differ from stipulated probabilities
labs.accessibleFallback: Editable probability table and computed values with formulas

labs.title: Code a tiny alphabet
labs.readout: Prefix tree, code lengths, expected length and entropy
labs.invariant: No leaf code is prefix of another; Kraft sum <= 1
labs.pitfalls: Entropy is a lower bound on ideal average length, not an achieved length for every finite code
labs.accessibleFallback: Tree as indented text and full encode/decode transcript

labs.title: Follow the best-response arrows
labs.readout: Pure equilibrium cells and expected payoff lines
labs.invariant: Marked pure equilibria pass every unilateral deviation check
labs.pitfalls: An equilibrium need not maximize joint payoff
labs.accessibleFallback: Payoff table with best-response labels and keyboard-selectable cells

labs.title: Count the same ballots three ways
labs.readout: Plurality, Borda and pairwise outcomes with cycle indicator
labs.invariant: Every ballot ranks each option once; totals reconcile with voter count
labs.pitfalls: Arrow theorem applies to stated ranking and fairness axioms, not a claim all voting is pointless
labs.accessibleFallback: Ballot table, pairwise count table and textual winner explanations

labs.title: Two tones and a beat envelope
labs.readout: Wave sum, envelope period and exact frequency difference
labs.invariant: For equal-amplitude sinusoidal tones, algebraic superposition identity holds
labs.pitfalls: The simple model ignores timbre and hearing context
labs.accessibleFallback: Numeric sample table, waveform description, optional muted audio and no autoplay

labs.title: Stress-test a toy network model
labs.readout: Outcome spread, sensitivity summary and model assumption card
labs.invariant: Node count bounded by graph size; fixed seed reproduces a run
labs.pitfalls: Simulation explores chosen rule, not real-world social behavior or causal impact
labs.accessibleFallback: Adjacency list, per-step state table and numeric sensitivity results
